title: Microsoft Authenticator: iCloud backup and restore of account entries on iOS
summary: The recovery advice omits Microsoft's exception for passkeys saved in a synced credential manager: a new passkey might not be needed. The reassurance that no organisational sign-in credential moves also goes beyond the documented statement that only the work account name is restored.

claims.claim: Microsoft Authenticator on iOS supports iCloud backup and recovery of account entries on a new phone.
claims.quote: When you get a new phone, you can recover supported account entries and continue using secure sign-in methods by backing up and restoring these methods.

claims.claim: If passkeys are enforced, a passkey must be set up for the new phone before removing the old device.
claims.quote: If the passkey was saved to a synced credential manager, such as Microsoft Password Manager, Google Password Manager, or Apple iCloud Keychain, you might not need to create a new passkey. Verify the passkey is available before removing the old device.
claims.fix: Replace the clause beginning 'Learn says that if passkeys are enforced' with: 'Learn says that if passkeys are enforced, set up a passkey for the new phone before removing the old device; if the passkey was saved to a synced credential manager, a new passkey might not be needed, but verify it is available before removing the old device.' Keep the transfer-page citation.

claims.claim: After opting in to passkey profiles, the self-service setting is at Microsoft Entra admin center > Entra ID > Security > Authentication methods > Policies > Passkey (FIDO2) > Configure > Allow self-service set up.
claims.quote: Browse to Entra ID > Security > Authentication methods > Policies. Select Passkey (FIDO2). Select the link in the banner text to opt-in to using passkeys profiles. On the Configure tab, set Allow self-service set up to Yes.

claims.claim: PATCH /v1.0/policies/authenticationMethodsPolicy/authenticationMethodConfigurations/fido2 updates the FIDO2 policy, including self-service registration.
claims.quote:
PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/policies/authenticationMethodsPolicy/authenticationMethodConfigurations/fido2
"isSelfServiceRegistrationAllowed": true

claims.claim: Configuring the passkey row requires at least Authentication Policy Administrator.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Entra admin center as at least an Authentication Policy Administrator.

claims.claim: The passkey row governs tenant-level self-service passkey registration, not Authenticator backup.
claims.quote: If set to No, users can't register a passkey by using Security info, even if passkeys (FIDO2) are enabled by the Authentication methods policy. This setting is a global policy; it's not on the profile level.

claims.claim: The Graph request-body property that controls passkey self-service registration is isSelfServiceRegistrationAllowed.
claims.quote: isSelfServiceRegistrationAllowed | Boolean | Determines if users can register new passkeys (FIDO2).

claims.claim: Once administrators opt in to passkey profiles, they cannot opt out.
claims.quote: After you opt in to enable passkey profiles, you can't opt out.

claims.claim: The cited Configure-tab instructions follow the step to opt in to passkey profiles.
claims.quote: Select the link in the banner text to opt-in to using passkeys profiles. ... On the Configure tab, set Allow self-service set up to Yes.

claims.where: rationale: risk; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: No organisational sign-in credential moves to iCloud because only the work account name is restored.
claims.quote: Searched: Authenticator backup TOTP credentials iCloud; Authenticator backup Graph configuration. Read transfer page and roadmap. The transfer page states what is restored, not a complete inventory of what is uploaded; the record describes account-name and TOTP-credential backup without this exclusion.
claims.fix: Replace the risk rationale with 'Low. Backup is a user-side iCloud setting, and for work or school accounts Learn says only the account name is restored.' In Data exposure, remove 'so no organisational sign-in credential is described as moving to iCloud'. Do not infer an upload exclusion from restore behaviour.

claims.claim: The backup stores one-time-code credentials in the user's iCloud backup.
claims.quote: using iCloud and iCloud Keychain. This enables secure, end-to-end encrypted backup of account names and TOTP credentials.

claims.claim: The sources do not state whether this account-backup change alters existing behaviour for users who do nothing.
claims.quote: Searched: Authenticator iOS improved backup restore automatically default minimum version administrator role. Read record and transfer page. Neither specifies migration of existing backup settings; the June 2026 announcement describes a separate device-bound passkey restore-flow improvement.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions

claims.quote: To back up Authenticator on an iOS device, enable iCloud Drive, Keychain, and Backup for Authenticator. ... Turn on the Authenticator toggle.

claims.claim: Nothing is documented as changing for people outside the described backup-and-new-phone scenario.
claims.quote: Searched: Authenticator iOS improved backup restore automatically default minimum version administrator role. Read record and transfer page: their account-backup descriptions concern backing up and setting up a new phone; neither describes other users' behaviour changing.

claims.claim: Learn tells users to contact their administrator or help desk if self-service passkey setup is not allowed.
claims.quote: If your IT admin doesn't allow self-service passkey setup, contact your admin or help desk for the approved recovery or registration process.
